html:
Old Calabar was a group of trading towns of the Efik people on the Calabar and Cross rivers, in what is now south-eastern Nigeria. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900. The modern city of Calabar grew from these towns.

The main towns, Duke Town and Creek Town, were run by merchant families and by the Ekpe society, a secret society of leading men that enforced debts and laws. Calabar was one of the busiest ports of the Atlantic slave trade in the 1700s, buying captives from the interior, many through the Aro.

After the slave trade ended, Calabar sold palm oil to British firms. Scottish Presbyterian missionaries came in 1846, among them later Mary Slessor. Britain made the area a protectorate in 1884, and Calabar served as the capital of the Oil Rivers and Niger Coast protectorates before Lagos took over.
